releases.name: v0.17.0 — clear the round
releases.body:
- **Clear** in the notes header removes every unsent note in the round; each page
  group also has its own **Clear**. One **Undo** restores the whole removed batch.
- Keep delivered history, **Restore last round** and page-local drafts. A pending
  retry batch is dropped only after inline confirmation when clearing the round.
- Browser protocol 8 requires matching companion files: reload the Chrome extension
  and restart OpenCode after updating.


## Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Reload the Annotate Chrome extension and restart OpenCode after updating.

releases.name: v0.16.1 — picking inside frames
releases.body:
- Fix picking and text selection inside same-origin iframes, legacy framesets and
  nested frames. Reveal and page markers find notes in frames after a reload.
- Record each note's frame in a `Frame:` line in delivered Markdown. Cross-origin
  frames show a clear message instead of silently failing to pick.
- Browser protocol 7 requires matching companion files: reload the Chrome extension
  and restart OpenCode after updating.


## Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Reload the Annotate Chrome extension and restart OpenCode after updating.

releases.name: v0.16.0 — /ref moves to Another
releases.body:
- **Breaking:** remove `/ref`, `/ref --all`, `/ref --tui` and the agent session
  search/read tools. Conversation references now belong to Another; Another 0.28.0
  ships a cross-agent `/ref`; install it and run `another setup`.
- Existing `opencode.json(c)` plugin entries keep working, including option sync.
  Remove any `annotate_session_*` permission rules. Reply, document and webpage
  annotation remain in Annotate.


## Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Restart OpenCode after updating.

releases.name: v0.15.0 — browser rounds and automatic connection
releases.body:
- Collect browser annotations across pages in one round, grouped by page in the panel
  and in one Send/Copy message. Keep page-local drafts, off-page note actions and global
  round recovery. Browser protocol 6 uses review envelope v2 with per-note pages.
- Register the Chrome native host and current/new sessions automatically. Resolve the
  real Node.js executable during setup; no separate host-install or pairing command is
  needed in normal use. Discover new sessions faster and share overlapping checks.
- Replace `/annotate-web` with `/annotate <url-or-html>`, and remove `/annotate-last`;
  plain `/annotate` still reviews the latest completed reply.
- Keep Send and Copy instead as separate actions. Choose destinations in one automatically
  refreshed, filterable picker with current titles and activity/creation/title sorting.
- Create empty OpenCode sessions from the extension without a prompt or model turn.
  Disconnect/reconnect delivery without losing drafts or retries, and reconnect restarted
  receivers by stable provider/session identity, carrying retries to the replacement.
- Continue after confirmed text/browser annotation sends with `steer` / `resume: true`:
  idle sessions start immediately; running turns receive feedback at the next boundary.
- Preserve Safari's existing sandboxed, copy-only boundary. Reload the Chrome extension
  after updating; protocol and review-envelope changes require matching companion files.

## Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

Reload the Annotate Chrome extension and restart OpenCode after updating.

releases.name: 0.14.0 — references as prompts
releases.body:
## References as prompts

`/ref` now submits the referenced conversation, your comment and any inline annotations
as **one ordinary user prompt**, rather than a compact reference item.

- Press **Ctrl+T** in the reference picker or use `/ref --tui <title or session ID>`
  to annotate the snapshot in the bundled reviewer.
- Confirming continues an existing conversation. Before the first message, references
  wait without starting the assistant; several can be added before you write.
- `/ref` works from OpenCode home, creating a destination only after confirmation.
- Historical text stays quoted and bounded, with source IDs and timestamps. Switching
  tabs does not redirect delivery.

Existing annotation/browser commands and their delivery behavior are unchanged.
Safari remains copy-only. No cross-agent hc functionality or third-party toolbar
artwork is included.

### Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
```

### Update

```sh
opencode plugin update @nxxxsooo/opencode-annotate@latest
opencode plugin list
```

Keep existing plugin options. Run `/reload` if the command list has not refreshed.
The npm package includes the native reviewer for macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64
and Windows x64. Safari support is source/build support, not a signed application.

### Verification

Release CI builds and checks all five native targets plus the Safari converter/Xcode
gate. Isolated OpenCode tests verify prompt admission and continuation intent while
suppressing model execution. The user confirmed the development prompt flow worked.
